overview.description: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

history.origins: Partnership pinochle shares the same roots as pinochle generally: either as a cousin of Binokel with both evolving from bezique, or from the Swiss and South German game Binocle or Binokel. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and misspelled as 'pinochle'; it became a favorite among American Jewish and Irish immigrants. Partnership auction pinochle emerged as the standard form in the United States in the early 20th century.
timeline: Late 19th century: German immigrants brought Binokel to America; game became known as pinochle. Early 20th century: partnership auction pinochle popular in the United States.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.
nullReasons.cultural: No specific cultural or regional significance documented beyond its origins.

setup.deck: 48-card Pinochle deck: twelve cards per suit (two each of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace) in all four French suits.
setup.equipment: Standard 48-card Pinochle deck (two copies of 9 through Ace in each suit).
setup.dealing: All 48 cards dealt clockwise in packets of three or four, starting with the player to the dealer's left (eldest hand). Each player receives 12 cards. Deal rotates clockwise each hand.

rules.objective: Reach the agreed target score (typically 1000 or 1500) by combining meld points and trick points. Bid to name trump; the bidding team must make at least their bid (meld plus trick points) or be set.
rules.gameplay: Deal 12 cards each. Auction: players bid in turn; high bidder declares trump. All players meld (runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds); points counted. High bidder leads; follow suit if possible, must trump if void; identical cards rank first-played. Trick points plus meld must meet or exceed the bid for the bidding team. First partnership to reach target wins.

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Auction until three players pass; high bidder declares trump.

phases.label: Melding
phases.notes: Bid winner melds first; all display melds; points counted then cards returned to hand.

phases.label: Play tricks
phases.notes: High bidder leads; 12 tricks; follow suit, trump when void, overtake when required.

play_card.description: Play one card to the trick. Must follow lead suit if possible; if void in suit must play trump if able; when trump is led must play higher trump if able (overtake). First card of identical rank played wins.
play_card.constraints: Legal when it is your turn in the play phase. Must follow suit or trump; must overtake when required by rules.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.description: Pass (do not bid) in the auction. Once a player passes they may not bid again that round.
pass.constraints: Legal during bidding phase when it is your turn to bid.

bid.description: Make a bid (points you expect your side to make from meld and tricks). Each bid must be higher than the previous; minimum opening bid typically 150. High bidder declares trump.
bid.constraints: Legal during bidding when it is your turn. Bid must exceed current high bid; bids in multiples of 10.

meld.description: Lay down melds (runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds, dix) face-up for count. Bid winner melds first; all players meld. Cards may be used in one meld per type.
meld.constraints: Legal during meld phase after trump is declared. Meld points are totalled; then cards returned to hand for play.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must play higher trump when trumping if possible; when trump is led must head the trick if able.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: Bid winner melds first; all players meld; points counted.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: High bidder leads first trick; thereafter trick winner leads.

customActions.description: Deal all 48 cards: 12 to each player, clockwise in packets of three or four, starting with eldest hand.
customActions.constraints: Legal only for the dealer at start of hand.

engine.handRankingSystem: Trick ranking: A 10 K Q J 9 in trump; led suit then trump for trick winner.
engine.deckDescription: A single 48-card Pinochle deck: four French suits, each with two copies of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace. Partnership Pinochle uses one pack; players bid, meld, and play tricks in teams; scoring combines meld and trick points.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each have twelve cards (two each of 9 through Ace). Trump is determined by bid; marriages and other melds require suit and rank; following suit applies in play.
engine.rankDescription: Pinochle order: 9 low, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace high; Jack of trump (Jick) and Queen of trump (Spad) are the two highest trumps. Rank determines trick winners and meld scoring (marriage, run, pinochle).
engine.dealPattern: 3 or 4 cards at a time clockwise, eldest hand first; all 48 cards, 12 per player.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: All 48 cards are dealt at start of hand; there is no draw-from-stock during play.

notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Trick-taking and melding game; no play-to-capture or fishing mechanic.

synthesis.shortDescription: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

scoring.description: Meld points (runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds, dix) plus trick points (aces and tens 10 each, kings and queens 5 each, last trick 10). Bidding team must make at least their bid or be set (bid subtracted).
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach the agreed target score (typically 1000 or 1500) wins the game.

nullReasons.cardValues: Trick and meld point values are in scoring.description; cardValues reserved for per-rank breakdown when used.
